Criterion: Verify that the operator and maintenance manuals for the air vehicle and the targeted tanker(s)/receiver(s) document safe operation of the aerial refueling systems. Standard: The manuals identify the proper operator and maintenance instructions/information and placards noting restrictions and limitations in the use of the air vehicle's aerial refueling system(s) under all operating conditions (ground/in-flight; normal/emergency). Flight procedures address all applicable factors involved in aerial refueling operation including, but not limited to: a. Day versus night. b. With and without night vision goggle(s) (NVG). c. Rendezvous methods. d. Formation techniques. e. Approved airspeed/altitude envelopes:
(1) Tanker/receiver contacts.
(2) Opening/extending system.
(3) System in open/extended position.
(4) Returning system to stowed/retracted position. f. Receiver contact/closure rate limits (probe-drogue systems only) and receiver closure/fall back rate limits once engaged. g. For boom systems, envelopes (elevation, roll/azimuth, extension) for receiver contact, receiver disconnect, and boom control limits. h. Single versus multiple aircraft operations. i. Fuel transfer restrictions (e.g., flow rates/delivery pressures). j. Reverse aerial refueling. k. Operational restrictions. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include inspection and review of documentation. Aerial refueling procedures are identified and confirmed through inspection of appropriate documentation. References: JSSG-2001: 3.1.1.1.1, 3.4.6.2.1, 3.4.6.2.2 ATP-3.3.4.2 NATO STANAG 3971

Standard: Flight and maintenance manuals document normal and emergency procedures for the AR systems including applicable limitations, restrictions, warnings, cautions, notes, and allowable environmental conditions. Air vehicles approved by Aerial Refueling Certification Agency to AR with the platform including associated clearance levels and defined AR envelopes are identified. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of draft flight and maintenance manuals and flight test procedures verify AR procedures, allowable conditions, and refueling envelopes are documented. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
(2) Examination of flight and maintenance manuals verify AR procedures, allowable conditions and refueling envelopes are documented. Test.
  (1) Flight test: Flight test verifies procedures are accurate and usable.
